result.planSummary: Applied the impl-lead ruling by surfacing unambiguous project-shell refresh ownership in source summaries, hiding project-shell refresh controls for project-scoped sources unless exactly one current process working-copy target exists, and keeping process-surface refresh behavior unchanged while preserving pending refresh as operation metadata.

changedFiles.reason: Extended source attachment summaries with optional project-shell refresh target count metadata.
Computed project-shell refresh target counts from current process material refs and attached them to project-scoped source summaries.
Hidden project-shell refresh/rehydration controls unless the source is process-scoped or has exactly one current process target.
Added focused zero/one/many project-shell refresh-control coverage while preserving pending refresh metadata behavior.
Added focused shell-bootstrap coverage proving project source summaries expose the target-count state the UI now relies on.

findingsFixed: Project-shell stale/not_hydrated rows no longer falsely offer refresh when zero or multiple current process targets exist.
Project-shell refresh remains available when ownership of the working copy is unambiguous via exactly one current process target.
Pending refresh stayed modeled as refresh metadata rather than a fifth hydration state.

result.recommendedNextStep: Proceed to verification with attention on the new project-shell target-count behavior and confirm the later cross-process project-level target-selection story can replace this gating when designed.
